lessons.title: Meet the crew
lessons.focus: Use a polite morning greeting, give your name and role with ～です, and ask a worker's name before confirming a role. The topic particle は is pronounced wa. At the end of ～です, か makes a question; お makes なまえ polite when asking someone else's name. Read the short lines in hiragana before introducing site kanji.
lessons.scene: A supervisor and carpenter meet at the morning check-in
terms: おはようございます|good morning (polite)
おなまえ|name (polite when asking someone)
よろしくおねがいします|I look forward to working with you
dialogue: おはようございます。|Good morning.
おはようございます。|Good morning.
わたしは さとうです。|I am Sato.
げんばかんとくです。|I am the site supervisor.
おなまえは なんですか。|What is your name?
わたしは たなかです。|I am Tanaka.
だいくですか。|Are you a carpenter?
はい、だいくです。|Yes, I am a carpenter.
たなかさん、よろしくおねがいします。|Tanaka, I look forward to working with you.
こちらこそ、よろしくおねがいします。|Likewise, I look forward to working with you.

lessons.title: Who is on site?
lessons.focus: Use こちら for a person near the speaker and ask どなたですか politely. A role can be given with ～です. Japanese often omits a subject that is clear from context. Treat きました as a fixed 'arrived' phrase for now; past forms are taught later.
lessons.scene: At the morning check-in, Yamada stands next to Sato; Sato asks Tanaka to introduce Yamada
terms: あたらしい かた|new person (polite)
dialogue: こちらは どなたですか。|Who is this person?
やまださんです。|This is Yamada.
やまださんは だいくですか。|Is Yamada a carpenter?
いいえ、でんきこうじの たんとうです。|No, Yamada is in charge of electrical work.
あたらしい かたですか。|Is this person new?
はい、きょう きました。|Yes, this person arrived today.
やまださん、よろしくおねがいします。|Yamada, I look forward to working with you.

lessons.title: Name the tool
lessons.focus: Point out a tool with これ (this near me) or それ (that near you). この and その go before a noun; they change with the speaker's position. Ask なんですか to identify it. の marks ownership or connects nouns, as in どうぐの はこ (tool box); ～のです can mean 'X's one' without repeating the object. Japanese often uses someone's name while speaking to them, where English says 'your'. も means 'also'.
lessons.scene: New helper Kobayashi checks tools with Sato at the morning storage area; the hammer is near Kobayashi and the box and saw are near Sato
terms: この|this near me (before a noun)
その|that near you (before a noun)
dialogue: これは なんですか。|What is this?
それは かなづちです。|That is a hammer.
この かなづちは さとうさんの どうぐですか。|Is this hammer your tool?
はい、わたしの どうぐです。|Yes, it is my tool.
その はこは なんですか。|What is that box?
どうぐの はこです。|It is a tool box.
その のこぎりも さとうさんのですか。|Is that saw also yours?
はい、わたしのです。|Yes, it is mine.

lessons.title: Count the crew and boxes
lessons.focus: Ask なんにん for a number of people and いくつ for a number of general items. ふたり counts two people; ふたつ counts two items. Keep the people counter separate from the item counter. The noun before は is the topic of the question. と joins Tanaka and one other person.
lessons.scene: Sato checks the morning roster with Tanaka and Ito, the two carpenters on this shift; two boxes are in storage and one is at the work site
dialogue: きょう、だいくは なんにんですか。|How many carpenters are here today?
ふたりです。|Two people.
たなかさんと もうひとりですか。|You and one more person, Tanaka?
はい、いとうさんです。|Yes, the other person is Ito.
そうこの はこは いくつですか。|How many boxes are in storage?
ふたつです。|Two boxes.
げんばの はこは いくつですか。|How many boxes are at the work site?
ひとつです。|One box.

lessons.title: Find a person or a tool
lessons.focus: Ask どこに for the location of someone or something. Use います for a person or animal and あります for an inanimate item. に marks the place where the person or item exists; Xの なかに means inside X.
lessons.scene: Sato and Kobayashi locate Tanaka, Yamada, and Sato's hammer before the shift starts
dialogue: たなかさんは どこに いますか。|Where is Tanaka?
そうこに います。|Tanaka is in the storage room.
わたしの かなづちは どこに ありますか。|Where is my hammer?
そうこの なかに あります。|It is inside the storage room.
やまださんも そうこに いますか。|Is Yamada also in the storage room?
いいえ、げんばに います。|No, Yamada is at the work site.

lessons.title: Where work happens
lessons.focus: Use に for where a person or object is: げんばに います. Use で for where a task happens: げんばで さぎょうします. さぎょうします means carry out work or a task. Ask どこに for existence and どこで for an action. Do not swap the particles.
lessons.scene: Later that morning, Sato asks Tanaka where Kobayashi is, where each worker will carry out tasks, and where Sato's saw is kept
terms: に|at; in (place where someone or something is)
さぎょうします|carry out work; work on a task (polite)
dialogue: こばやしさんは どこに いますか。|Where is Kobayashi?
げんばに います。|Kobayashi is at the work site.
たなかさんは きょう どこで さぎょうしますか。|Where will you carry out your work today, Tanaka?
そうこで さぎょうします。|I will work in the storage room.
こばやしさんは どこで さぎょうしますか。|Where will Kobayashi work on the task?
げんばで さぎょうします。|Kobayashi will work at the site.
わたしの のこぎりは どこに ありますか。|Where is my saw?
そうこに あります。|It is in the storage room.
